name: at
description: Schedules a one-time command to run at a specific time — cron for "once", not "always".

flags.description: Read the commands from a file.

examples.output:
at> reboot
at> <EOT>
job 4 at Sat Jan 12 10:45:00 2025
examples.explanation: Schedules a reboot in 30 minutes: type the command, end with Ctrl+D.
One-shot job at 03:00 tonight (requires the atd service running).
Lists pending jobs with their IDs.

about: at jobs run once via the atd daemon, with the environment captured at submission time (better than cron's minimal env). Jobs are queued in /var/spool/cron/atjobs/. If atd is not running, jobs silently wait — check systemctl status atd.
mistakes: Forgetting Ctrl+D to finish input — the prompt just keeps waiting.
Assuming atd runs — minimal servers often lack the at package.
